updating-controlled-row-sets.label: Updating Multiple Columns and Rows
updating-controlled-row-sets.summary: Learn how to update multiple columns and rows in a SQL table using controlled conditions to ensure data integrity.

try_updating_controlled_row_sets_sketch0.title: Correct Two Fields on One Item
try_updating_controlled_row_sets_sketch0.prompt: The audit approved two changes for item `3`: its price should become `50.00` and its status should become `inactive`. Apply both assignments in one scoped `UPDATE`. In `query.sql`, verify the resulting price and status for item 3. To test it in the workspace, run `operations.sql` before `query.sql`; the query file only reads the resulting database state.
try_updating_controlled_row_sets_sketch0.hint: Keep the related assignments together and restrict the change to one id.

help.concept: One UPDATE can apply several related assignments to the same approved row.
help.hint_1: Use one SET list for both changes.

single-choice-1.title: Understanding Multiple Column Updates
single-choice-1.prompt: What is the purpose of using the `SET` clause in an `UPDATE` statement?
single-choice-1.hint: Think about how the `SET` clause affects the columns in a table.

help.concept: The `SET` clause specifies which columns to update and their new values.
help.hint_1: The `SET` clause is used to assign new values to columns.
help.hint_2: It allows you to update one or more columns in a table.

options.a: To select specific rows to update
options.b: To specify the columns and their new values
options.c: To delete rows from a table

single-choice-2.title: Purpose of WHERE Clause
single-choice-2.prompt: Why is it important to use a `WHERE` clause in an `UPDATE` statement?
single-choice-2.hint: Consider what happens if you don't use a `WHERE` clause.

help.concept: The `WHERE` clause limits the rows affected by the `UPDATE`.
help.hint_1: Without a `WHERE` clause, all rows in the table could be updated.
help.hint_2: It ensures only specific rows are updated.

options.a: To update all rows in the table
options.b: To limit the update to specific rows
options.c: To delete rows from the table

multi-choice-1.title: Benefits of Compound WHERE Conditions
multi-choice-1.prompt: Which benefits can a well-written compound WHERE condition provide in an UPDATE? Select all that apply.
multi-choice-1.hint: Consider how compound conditions affect the update operation.

help.concept: Compound WHERE conditions combine criteria so a row is changed only when it satisfies the complete target rule.
help.hint_1: Think about row selection, not the number of SET assignments.
help.hint_2: The WHERE condition defines the mutation boundary.

options.b: It can require several criteria before a row is targeted.
options.c: It can narrow the mutation to the approved row set when the criteria are correct.
options.d: It automatically creates a backup table.

practice-compound-update-scope.title: Practice: Update a Compound Target Set
practice-compound-update-scope.prompt: The test Kitchen catalog is being retired. Change the status of Kitchen rows that are test data to `archived`. Use one scoped `UPDATE` whose condition requires both parts of that target. In `query.sql`, verify the affected rows. To test it in the workspace, run `operations.sql` before `query.sql`; the query file only reads the resulting database state.
practice-compound-update-scope.hint: Neither category alone nor the test flag alone is narrow enough.

help.concept: A compound WHERE condition expresses a multi-part business approval.
help.hint_1: Both target conditions belong in the same update.
help.hint_2: Verify the exact target set afterward.

sketch1.title: One UPDATE can change related fields together
sketch1.bodyMarkdown:
When one approved correction changes several fields on the same rows, keep those assignments in one `UPDATE`.

```sql
UPDATE inventory_items
SET price = 5.99, status = 'active'
WHERE id = 2;
```

The `SET` list describes the approved changes. The `WHERE` condition describes which rows may receive them.

sketch2.title: A compound condition expresses the full approval
sketch2.bodyMarkdown:
Sometimes one condition is not enough to identify the approved set.

```sql
UPDATE inventory_items
SET status = 'inactive'
WHERE category = 'Decor' AND is_test = 1;
```

Both conditions matter. Removing either one would widen the mutation beyond the intended group.
